_notes: Unofficial: Roblox doesn't document FFlags. Everything here comes from community sources (Bloxstrap/Voidstrap, GitHub fflag repos, MaximumADHD's client-extracted tracker).
[KNOWN] = corroborated by multiple sources. [ASSUMPTION] = real flag, effect inferred from naming/usage. [UNKNOWN] = real flag, effect unclear.
[CAUTION] = documented as exploit-capable; reference only, not a recommendation to use (ban risk).
Recommended values are community convention, not tested. Flags get renamed/removed without notice -- treat as perishable.

popular_fflags.description: [KNOWN] Sets the client's target/max framerate. Extremely widely used and consistent across every source checked.
[ASSUMPTION] Appears to gate whether the client enforces a hard 240fps ceiling regardless of DFIntTaskSchedulerTargetFps; setting False is the community convention to allow uncapping above 240.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to control whether extended framerate cap options are exposed in the in-game settings menu.
[KNOWN] Forces the client to prefer the Direct3D 11 rendering backend.
[KNOWN] Disables the Direct3D 11 backend, used together with a Prefer flag to force Vulkan or OpenGL.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to force D3D11 running at Feature Level 10, intended as a compatibility fallback for older GPUs.
[KNOWN] Forces the client to prefer the Vulkan rendering backend when paired with disabling D3D11.
[KNOWN] Forces the client to prefer the OpenGL rendering backend, generally used as a legacy-hardware fallback.
[UNKNOWN] Name suggests enabling compute-shader support on D3D10-class hardware; no source explains real-world effect or risk.
[KNOWN] Disables post-processing effects (bloom, color correction, etc.) client-side. One of the most consistently cited performance flags.
[KNOWN] Replaces the skybox with a flat gray color, cited in multiple performance/leak lists.
[KNOWN] Controls shadow darkness/intensity; setting to 0 is the standard way to effectively remove shadows.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to pause the voxel-based lighting update system to reduce GPU load; naming and community usage are consistent but not independently confirmed.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to control fade distance for voxel-based lighting transitions; consistently paired with the voxelizer pause flag in community configs.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to force the legacy Voxel lighting technology instead of Future/ShadowMap, for lower-end performance.
[UNKNOWN] Appears related to forcing the newest ('Future') lighting pipeline phase, but no source explains the exact mechanism.
[KNOWN] Enables manual override of texture quality, used together with DFIntTextureQualityOverride.
[KNOWN] Sets forced texture quality level (lower = blurrier/lower VRAM use).
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to skip mipmap levels to reduce VRAM usage; sign/magnitude of the value varies between sources (some use -1, some use 1), so treat exact value as unverified.
[ASSUMPTION] Community sources describe this as controlling terrain texture array detail; lower values reduce quality/memory use. Exact mechanism not independently confirmed.
[KNOWN] Maximum distance at which terrain grass renders.
[KNOWN] Minimum distance before grass begins rendering.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to control density of individual grass strands rendered.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to toggle physically-based light falloff calculations vs. legacy attenuation.
[KNOWN] Maximum number of local light updates processed per frame.
[KNOWN] Minimum number of local light updates processed per frame.
[KNOWN] Fade-in duration in milliseconds for local light updates; setting to 0 makes lights appear instantly instead of animating in.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to enable a faster GPU-side light culling path; cited repeatedly in performance-flag packs but not explained in detail anywhere.

[KNOWN] Directly overrides the internal Fast Render Model quality level, bypassing the normal 1-10 in-game graphics slider mapping (which maps to internal values like 3, 2, 6, 7, 11, 14, 15, 17, 18, 21 per community-documented tables).
[KNOWN] Sets the default in-game graphics quality slider level (1-10) on launch.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to restrict maximum object/geometry render (culling) distance.
[KNOWN] Enables/disables the global wind simulation system affecting things like foliage sway.
[UNKNOWN] Appears in multiple leak lists related to CSG (union/mesh) level-of-detail switching, but exact behavior and units aren't documented anywhere reliable.
[UNKNOWN] Name suggests enabling compression for async HTTP asset requests; effect not explained in any source found.

[KNOWN] Sets the network MTU size used for client packets; widely included in 'low ping' flag packs, though claimed optimal values vary a lot between sources (900-1500), which is itself a sign most of these values are guesses rather than tested.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to skip certain splash/loading screens to launch games faster.
[KNOWN] Displays a persistent FPS counter overlay.
[KNOWN] Changes Alt+Enter to trigger true exclusive fullscreen instead of the default borderless behavior.
[KNOWN] Disables Windows DPI scaling for the client, which some users apply to fix blurry UI on scaled displays.
[KNOWN] Part of a documented set of flags that disable various Roblox telemetry/analytics counters client-side. Commonly bundled with the other telemetry-disable flags below.
[KNOWN] Disables a telemetry stat channel; bundled with the other telemetry-disable flags.
[KNOWN] Disables telemetry event ingestion; bundled with the other telemetry-disable flags.
[KNOWN] Disables a telemetry data-point channel; bundled with the other telemetry-disable flags.
[KNOWN] Disables the v2 telemetry counter channel; bundled with the other telemetry-disable flags.
[KNOWN] Disables the v2 telemetry event channel; bundled with the other telemetry-disable flags.
[KNOWN] Disables the v2 telemetry stat channel; bundled with the other telemetry-disable flags.
[UNKNOWN] Appears in leak lists near other facial-animation LOD (facs = facial capture system) flags; no source explains exact effect.
[UNKNOWN] Appears alongside DFIntAnimationLodFacsDistanceMin; presumed to be the far-distance cutoff for facial animation detail, not independently confirmed.

[UNKNOWN] Appears in 'low ping' leaked-flag packs with no explanation. Given the name references skipping validation of join data, treat with caution rather than assuming it's purely cosmetic/performance-related.
[ASSUMPTION] Part of a cluster of flags ('Chrome') believed to control Roblox's newer in-game menu/UI system rollout.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to toggle bubble chat rendering being driven by the newer chat service.

[KNOWN] Controls how many missed physics steps the client will 'remember' and catch up on after a lag spike. Community sources note the physics engine won't go below 60 steps/sec through the normal UI, so this is set very high specifically to prevent physics slowdown during frame drops.
[UNKNOWN] Cited as related to physics simulation stability testing; no source explains the actual mechanism beyond the name.
[UNKNOWN] Name suggests disabling client-side network position extrapolation (predicting where other players will be between updates); effect and tradeoffs not independently confirmed.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to control whether the physics engine uses adaptive (variable) timestepping by default.

[CAUTION][UNKNOWN] Community sources claim setting this to -1 stops the client from replicating your own animations to the server (you still see them locally). Exact behavior unverified and this could look like desync/exploit behavior to anti-cheat or other players.
[CAUTION][UNKNOWN] Part of a trio of radius flags community sources describe as expanding the client's physics simulation radius to an extreme value. Purpose/side effects beyond that are unverified.
[CAUTION][UNKNOWN] See DFIntMinClientSimulationRadius; appears alongside it in the same flag trio in community sources.

[CAUTION][KNOWN] Documented in community repos as controlling collision-extent expansion in studs; setting it very negative is reported to let the client clip through thin walls/floors client-side. Explicitly labeled exploitable by the source that documents it -- using this can get an account banned in games with anti-cheat.
[KNOWN] Enables the Ctrl+Shift+G / Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+B family of keyboard shortcuts for hiding CoreGuis, ScreenGuis, and 3D-space GUIs.
[UNKNOWN] Takes a Roblox group ID as its value per community instructions; exact purpose relative to the GUI-hide toggles above is not explained.

[ASSUMPTION] Believed to control the delay in milliseconds before the fullscreen title bar auto-hides/triggers; community configs set it to a huge value (e.g. 3600000ms = 1 hour) to effectively disable it.
[UNKNOWN] Adjusts padding around rendered font sizes according to community sources; exact visual effect not independently confirmed.
[UNKNOWN] Community sources set this to a very small value; presumed to cap the length of kick-message text shown to the client, but not independently confirmed.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to set the minimum distance at which spatial voice chat volume begins falling off with distance.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to set the maximum distance at which spatial voice chat becomes inaudible.

[UNKNOWN] Appears in performance-flag packs alongside a matching LowQuality variant; naming suggests a pixel-size threshold below which shadow-casting objects are culled from the high-quality shadow map. Community configs set both to the max int value (2147483647), effectively disabling that threshold.
[UNKNOWN] See DFIntCullFactorPixelThresholdShadowMapHighQuality; the low-quality-map counterpart.
[UNKNOWN] Part of a small cluster of 'VisBugChecks' flags in community repos; presumed to be internal visibility/culling bug-detection instrumentation, not independently explained.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to hide your own character's particle effects while in first-person camera mode, reducing visual clutter/GPU load.
[UNKNOWN] Name suggests hiding the close button on the player list UI; not independently confirmed.
[KNOWN] Disables Roblox's automatic reconnect-on-disconnect behavior. Frequently paired with FStringReconnectDisabledReason, which sets custom text shown when reconnect is blocked.
[KNOWN] Toggles the modernized in-game escape menu redesign, part of a larger cluster of menu-versioning flags (v2/v3/'Chrome') that Roblox has used to stage this rollout.
[UNKNOWN] Appears in community chat/voice-related flag lists; presumed to gate some generation of the voice chat feature but not independently explained.
[ASSUMPTION] Name suggests fixing rounding/precision display of mouse sensitivity values in settings text.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to toggle whether system messages (join/leave, etc.) are included in automatic chat translation.

[KNOWN] A comma-separated list of locale codes (e.g. es_es, fr_fr, ja_jp) that Roblox's automatic chat translation supports. Community sources note English cannot be removed from translation regardless of this list.
[UNKNOWN] Presumed to control how many game tiles appear per row/feed on the Roblox home page grid; effect not independently confirmed.
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to gate an experimental version of the screenshot/video capture hotkey system.

[UNKNOWN] A real flag name seen in community lists (likely an internal joke reference, per the Star Wars naming), but no source explains what it actually controls. Treat with extra caution given the unexplained, dramatically-named nature.
[KNOWN] Forces in-experience text chat to be disabled client-side.
[UNKNOWN] Appears alongside the other facial-animation LOD distance flags; presumed to be a divisor affecting facial-capture visibility falloff, not independently confirmed.
[UNKNOWN] Presumed to control whether the default voice/text channel starts muted; not independently confirmed.
[KNOWN] Controls the rollout percentage (in per-mille, i.e. parts per thousand) of the experience-language-selection menu feature; setting to 0 removes that option from settings for the client.
[KNOWN] Sets the maximum camera zoom-out distance client-side. Community sources note it only takes effect in experiences that haven't set their own custom zoom limit via game settings.
[UNKNOWN] Name suggests gating an experiment (IXP = internal experimentation platform) related to mute toggles in the newer 'Chrome' UI; effect not independently confirmed.
[KNOWN] Toggles streaming of facial animation data (v2 of the system), letting the client reduce facial-animation network/processing load when disabled.
[KNOWN] Toggles Roblox's newer camera control scheme/input handling.
[KNOWN] Enables a version of directional audio occlusion (sound muffling through walls/objects).
[ASSUMPTION] Believed to enable an in-client audio output device selector (choosing which speaker/headset Roblox plays through).
[KNOWN] Controls the rate at which the client sends physics state updates to the server. Lower values reduce outgoing bandwidth but can make movement look less smooth to other players.
[KNOWN] Enables an on-screen network interpolation debugging overlay, toggled in-game with Ctrl+F8.
[KNOWN] Draws bounding boxes around all parts and humanoids for physics/hitbox debugging.

[CAUTION][UNKNOWN] Documented in community sources with no explanation beyond the name; relates to blocking large tool-weld manipulations in physics. Given it touches tool/weld physics, treat as potentially exploit-adjacent.
[CAUTION][UNKNOWN] Appears in community physics-exploit flag lists paired with a 'NonSolidFloor' counterpart; exact mechanism unexplained but grouped with other movement/force-manipulation flags.
[CAUTION][UNKNOWN] See DFIntSolidFloorPercentForceApplication; its counterpart for non-solid floor surfaces.
[UNKNOWN] Presumed to adjust depth bias used when rendering shadow maps (affects shadow acne/peter-panning artifacts); not independently confirmed.
[KNOWN] Forces a specific MSAA (multi-sample anti-aliasing) sample count, overriding the normal graphics-quality-driven setting.
[KNOWN] Scales down the resolution of composited avatar/character textures to reduce GPU and memory load.
